messages:
carmen: Quick pulse check — I ran a tiny bring-up across west/us-east/eu for embeddings + small-chat. Wanting to capture kernel-level notes and rough cost/perf before the full sweep.

duncan: nice. what hardware and quantization did you try?

carmen: L4, T4, A10G. baseline float32, and a 4-bit PTQ run for each. embed inputs are 32 tokens avg, small-chat prompt ~120 tokens + 64 gen. region: us-west, us-east, eu-west.

ben_ml: raw numbers from the short run (single GPU, steady-state, no batching for embeddings, batch=8 for chat):
- embeddings (qps): L4=210 qps, A10G=175 qps, T4=115 qps
- embeddings p50 latency: L4=6.2ms, A10G=8.5ms, T4=12.8ms
- small-chat (throughput, responses/min): L4=520 rpm (~8.7 qps), A10G=420 rpm (~7 qps), T4=260 rpm (~4.3 qps)
- small-chat p50 latency (end-to-end, seq=256): L4=18ms, A10G=25ms, T4=36ms

ben_ml: 4-bit PTQ added ~18-22% qps uplift for embeddings on L4/A10G, ~12% on T4. For small-chat, latency p50 improved ~12% on L4 with 4-bit, but we saw occasional token stalls on T4.

alice: kernel notes: L4 prefers the fused-attn kernel and a custom GEMM path. On A10G the fused kernel helps but we hit a memcpy hotspot with our KV cache layout in eu nodes. T4 falls back to the legacy attention kernel and the optimiser isn't picking the same launch configs -> explains extra p50.

alice: also saw that using continuous batching on L4 yields much better packing for small-chat. On T4, continuous batching increases jitter due to smaller compute headroom.

carmen: thanks — any region-specific oddities? I saw eu p50 ~+7ms vs us-west for small-chat on A10G.

eva: network+placement. our eu cluster had a slightly older runtime build (kernel selector v1.9 vs v2.0 in us-west) which picks a fallback kernel for some sequence lengths. that alone added ~5-8ms. scheduling also pinned processes to a different CPU topology in that region (NUMA effect).

ben_ml: snippet of the command I used for reproducibility:
```
./run_microbench --model small-chat-v1 --gpus L4,A10G,T4 --quant {none,ptq4} --seq 256 --batch 8 --warm 60 --run 300 --region us-west,us-east,eu-west
```

duncan: cost-ish: rough unit economics from the short run (very approximate): per-1M embedding queries: L4 ~ $9-$11, T4 ~ $8-$10 (lower per-hour but much slower => higher latency), A10G ~ $11-$13. For small-chat (tokenized billing) L4 came in slightly cheaper than A10G at our observed throughput thanks to better packing.

carmen: interesting — so T4 can look cheaper hourly but hurts throughput, making it worse for tail-sensitive products.

bench-bot: auto-summary: EMB: L4 > A10G > T4 (qps & p50). CHAT: L4 best latency & throughput, A10G competitive, T4 lagging. Quantization (4-bit PTQ) gives 10-22% perf uplift, with minor quality regressions on small-chat for some prompts. Region variance mostly due to kernel selector/runtime build and NUMA/cpu placement.

alice: open action items: (1) schedule a full sweep matrix (L4/T4/A10G x regions x quant modes) with consistent runtime build, (2) add a microkernel selector test in CI to detect fallbacks, (3) baseline prompt-level QA on 4-bit for small-chat to quantify regressions.

carmen: yep. I'll open a run ticket and assign. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
